verdicts.summary: The note says ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:369 now treats the resume as non-user, but does not follow what happens next. On a server restart, a never-started auto-resume run is no longer kept as a held, retryable message. It is now cancelled, and restart continuation skips never-started runs, so the resume is dropped without notice.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A thread fails with usage_limit while auto-resume is on. The worker dispatches 'Continue where you left off.' with createdBy 'agent' (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:76). 2) The run is created as 'starting' but has no provider turn yet (startedAt null), for example while the provider session or workspace is still starting. 3) The server shuts down or restarts. 4) In reconcile, unstartedRuns contains this run (ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:329-339). retryableMessageIds requires createdBy === 'user' (line 369), so the run is not retryable. It stays in `runs` and is emitted as status 'cancelled' (line 479). Before this commit it was moved to the held queue with its user_message item reset to pending (lines 399-441). 5) RestartContinuation ignores neverStarted runs (RestartContinuation.ts:129-130), so nothing continues the thread. Result: the auto-resume the user relied on never runs and the thread sits idle until someone notices. I did not confirm whether the worker re-arms afterwards. That depends on how the ProjectionStore latestRunId/status derivation treats a run cancelled before start (cancelledBeforeStart, RestartBackgroundNote.ts:182). Even if it does re-fire, the deterministic messageId `limit-resume:<identity>` is already used.
verdicts.consequence: After a restart that lands in the window between dispatch and the provider accepting the prompt, the usage-limit auto-resume is silently cancelled instead of being kept in the held queue.
